notes.maxzoom: 512 px tiles at z13 are 5.8 m a pixel at 53 N, the same as 256 px tiles at z14: the imagery is 10 m, so this is its native resolution with room to spare. The map overzooms past it.
notes.maxBadFraction: A scene whose window is more than this share cloud, shadow or no data (SCL) is not read past its SCL.
notes.select: Which coastal looks are read (fetch.py; --every-look reads them all). Per station of the tile, its levels at the overpasses are cut into bins equal steps, and each step is given perBin clear looks, the least cloudy first (the catalogue's tile cloud); a look found cloudy over the coast is replaced by the next. A step with fewer looks gives all it has: the lowest tides, rare at the overpass, are the ones that show the lowest flats dry. Each tide tail (the composite's candidates) is given tailLooks clear looks as well. About a third of the acquisitions, for the same spread of levels.
notes.composite: Per pixel, the median of the clean looks whose tide (at the pixel's station) is in the bottom lowPercentile or top highPercentile of that station's tides at Sentinel-2's overpass, from every season. Keeping to the summer looks where a pixel had enough of them made the sea blotchy (the choice changes from pixel to pixel with the clouds); the seasons' colours are kept apart instead by giving the land the one summer composite in both.
notes.tideZone: Where water ever reaches (wet in at least tideZoneMinWetShare of the clean looks, joined to the sea, not lush vegetation) and a margin round it, the image is tide-sorted; elsewhere both options share one summer composite, so land looks the same in both.
notes.heights: The rocks pilot's method (scripts/rockspilot/build_heights.py): each pixel's flip level between dry and wet against the tide, with its misfit; biasMetres is subtracted (the pilot measured +0.26 m against the OPW LiDAR).
